filesystem.description: File operations - read, write, search files in allowed directories. ~ and ~/jrvs-workspace are expanded at runtime.

brave-search.description: Web search via Brave. Add your API key above (https://brave.com/search/api/)

sqlite.description: Direct SQL access to JRVS memory database. Requires: pip install mcp-server-sqlite. $JRVS_DIR is set automatically to the JRVS project root.

slack.description: Slack integration. Replace the token and team ID with your real values — see _setup_instructions below.

memory.description: DISABLED: JRVS uses its built-in FAISS vector store for memory. This MCP server would create a parallel shadow store invisible to RAG retrieval.

_comment: Paths support ~ (home dir) and $ENV_VARS — they are expanded at runtime by JRVS.

setup_steps: 2. The command path '~/.local/bin/mcp-server-sqlite' is expanded automatically
3. Update the --db-path arg to point to your jarvis.db if your JRVS lives elsewhere
example_queries: SELECT title, url FROM documents ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 10
SELECT content FROM chunks WHERE content LIKE '%python%' LIMIT 5

setup_steps: 1. Go to https://api.slack.com/apps → Create New App → From scratch
2. Name it JRVS, pick your workspace, click Create App
3. OAuth & Permissions → Bot Token Scopes → add: channels:history, channels:read, chat:write, reactions:read, users:read, groups:read
4. Install to Workspace → Allow → copy the xoxb-... Bot Token
5. Get Team ID from Slack URL: app.slack.com/client/TXXXXXXX/...
6. Paste both into the env fields in the slack server config above

filesystem.setup_note: Add any directories you want JRVS to access to the args array. ~ is expanded to your home directory.
filesystem.security: Only directories listed in args are accessible.

setup_steps: 2. Add key to BRAVE_API_KEY env field above
brave-search.note: The built-in /websearch command works independently of this MCP server.
